title: Form Security and Accessibility knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Form Security and Accessibility”?
options: Form Security and Accessibility helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Form Security and Accessibility means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Form Security and Accessibility removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Form Security and Accessibility should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Form Security and Accessibility helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Form Security and Accessibility is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Treating submitted data as untrusted” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Treating submitted data as untrusted” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Treating submitted data as untrusted” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Treating submitted data as untrusted” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Treating submitted data as untrusted” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Treating submitted data as untrusted” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Treating submitted data as untrusted” under Form Security and Accessibility. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Form Security and Accessibility”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
